fields.name: meshes
fields.doc: List of meshes to focus on

fields.doc: Whether to include children when computing bounding boxes

fields.name: orientation
fields.doc:
Orientation vector indicating the direction from which to view the object
The camera will be positioned in this direction from the center of the bounding box

fields.name: distance
fields.doc:
Distance from the center of the bounding box to position the camera
If not specified, distance will be automatically calculated based on object size

fields.name: padding
fields.doc:
Padding multiplier to control spacing around objects when distance is auto-calculated
Higher values = more space around object (camera further away)
Lower values = tighter framing (camera closer)
Only applies when distance is not manually specified

fields.name: animationSpeed
fields.doc: Speed of camera animation in seconds

fields.name: ease
fields.doc: Easing curve of the focus animation: easeIn starts gently, easeOut ends gently, easeInOut does both; elastic, back and bounce overshoot.

members.summary: Focus camera on specified meshes from a specific angle with smooth animation.
members.doc:
Focus camera on specified meshes from a specific angle with smooth animation.
Computes the center of the bounding box of all meshes and positions the camera
at the specified orientation vector to look at the center.
Works only with ArcRotateCamera. Animation can be interrupted if called multiple times.

members.name: patterns
members.summary: Surface patterning: projecting a repeating motif across geometry and turning it into real shapes.
members.doc:
Surface patterning: projecting a repeating motif across geometry and turning it into real shapes.
This is how textured, perforated and faceted surfaces are produced without modelling each cell by
hand.

members.name: facePatterns
members.summary: Patterns applied across the surface of a face, laid out in the face's own parameter space so the cells follow its curvature rather than a flat grid projected onto it.
members.doc:
Patterns applied across the surface of a face, laid out in the face's own parameter space so the
cells follow its curvature rather than a flat grid projected onto it.

members.name: createPyramidSimpleAffectors

fields.name: faces
fields.doc: The faces on which to apply the pattern

fields.name: affectorPoints
fields.doc: The affector points affect the height of the pyramid elements. The distance is measured between a center point of the corner points and the attractor point. Then it is remapped to certain values.

fields.name: affectorRadiusList
fields.doc: The affector radius indicates the limit of affection. Cells heights that are further away from the affector than this radius will not be adjusted. If value is not provided, all affector points will use the radius of 10.

fields.name: affectorFactors
fields.doc:
The affector factors determine if a given affector attracts (value 0 to 1) or repulses (values -1 to 0) the default height of the pyramid elements.
If value is not provided, all affector points will use the factor of 1 and will thus attract the heights.

fields.name: uNumber
fields.doc: The nr of pyramids along u direction of the face

fields.name: vNumber
fields.doc: The nr of pyramids along v direction of the face

fields.name: defaultHeight
fields.doc: The default height for the pyramid if it is not affected by any of the affectors.

fields.name: affectMinHeight
fields.doc:
Min value to add to the height if affector factor is 1 or subtract from the height if affector factor is -1.
This adds to the height if the affector factor > 0 and subtracts from the height if the affector factor is < 0.

fields.name: affectMaxHeight
fields.doc:
Max value to add to the height if affector factor is 1 or subtract from the height if affector factor is -1.
This adds to the height if the affector factor > 0 and subtracts from the height if the affector factor is < 0.

fields.name: precision
fields.doc: Meshing precision of the drawn model. The lower the number the more precise the drawn model is. Keep in mind that output of this algorithm also contains pure occt shape that can be meshed separately in draw any async commands

members.name: babylon
members.summary: The BabylonJS side of the library: everything that lives in the rendered scene rather than in a CAD kernel.
members.doc:
The BabylonJS side of the library: everything that lives in the rendered scene rather than in a
CAD kernel. Meshes, nodes, cameras, lights, materials, textures, the scene itself, model import
and export, picking with rays, on-screen gizmos, the 2D GUI, decals, Gaussian splats and WebXR
are each behind their own property.

members.name: camera
members.summary: Cameras of the BabylonJS scene: `arcRotate` orbits a target and is the usual choice for looking at a model, `free` flies with keyboard and pointer, `target` looks at a point without user control.
members.doc:
Cameras of the BabylonJS scene: `arcRotate` orbits a target and is the usual choice for looking
at a model, `free` flies with keyboard and pointer, `target` looks at a point without user
control. The methods here set a camera's position, target, speed and clipping distances and
switch it between perspective and orthographic projection.

members.name: arcRotate
members.summary: The orbiting camera: it circles a target point at a distance, the way you would turn a product in your hands, and is the camera this library uses by default.
members.doc:
The orbiting camera: it circles a target point at a distance, the way you would turn a product in
your hands, and is the camera this library uses by default. Angles are given in degrees: `alpha`
around the vertical axis, `beta` down from the top.

members.name: create

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: Distance from the target the camera starts at, in scene units

fields.name: target
fields.doc: The point the camera looks at and orbits around

fields.name: alpha
fields.doc: The camera's angle around the vertical axis, in degrees

fields.name: beta
fields.doc: The camera's angle down from straight above, in degrees; 90 is level with the target

fields.name: lowerRadiusLimit
fields.doc:
The closest the camera may zoom to the target, in scene units; left out, there is no
limit

fields.name: upperRadiusLimit
fields.doc:
The farthest the camera may zoom from the target, in scene units; left out, there is no
limit

fields.name: lowerAlphaLimit
fields.doc:
The smallest angle around the vertical axis the camera may orbit to, in degrees; left
out, it orbits freely

fields.name: upperAlphaLimit
fields.doc:
The largest angle around the vertical axis the camera may orbit to, in degrees; left out,
it orbits freely

fields.name: lowerBetaLimit
fields.doc:
How close to straight above the camera may go, in degrees down from the top; 0 would look
straight down

fields.name: upperBetaLimit
fields.doc:
How close to straight below the camera may go, in degrees down from the top; 180 would
look straight up

fields.name: angularSensibilityX
fields.doc: How much pointer movement a horizontal orbit takes; lower turns faster

fields.name: angularSensibilityY
fields.doc: How much pointer movement a vertical orbit takes; lower turns faster

fields.name: panningSensibility
fields.doc: How much pointer movement a pan takes; lower pans faster, so lower it for large models

fields.name: wheelPrecision
fields.doc:
How much wheel movement a zoom step takes; lower zooms faster, so lower it for large
models

fields.name: maxZ
fields.doc: The farthest distance the camera draws, in scene units; anything beyond is not rendered

members.summary: Creates a camera that orbits `target` at distance `radius`, controlled by the pointer on the canvas, and adds it to the scene without activating it.
members.doc:
Creates a camera that orbits `target` at distance `radius`, controlled by the pointer on the
canvas, and adds it to the scene without activating it.

`alpha` and `beta` place it in degrees, `beta` counted down from straight above; the limits
fence how far it can zoom and orbit, and the sensibilities set how fast it reacts, lower
being faster.

and pointer, for walking through a scene rather than looking at one object.

members.name: decal
members.summary: Sticking images onto meshes, the way a label or a logo sits on a product.
members.doc:
Sticking images onto meshes, the way a label or a logo sits on a product. A geometry decal is a
thin clipped mesh hugging the surface, which works on any static mesh; a decal map paints into
the mesh's own texture space instead, adds no geometry, follows deformation and lets many
projections build up, but needs clean UV coordinates.

fields.doc: Mesh to project the decal onto. The decal is created as a clipped child mesh hugging the surface.

fields.doc: Image texture to project. Create it via texture image, and keep an alpha channel for cutout decals.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Position of the decal projector in world coordinates. Often picked from a ray/pick hit on the mesh.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: Direction the decal is projected along, in world coordinates. Usually the surface normal at the hit point.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Size of the decal box on each axis. The third value is the projection depth.

fields.name: angle
fields.doc: Angle to rotate the decal around the projection direction, in radians.

fields.name: cullBackFaces
fields.doc: Remove back faces from the decal mesh so it only sticks to faces pointing towards the projector.

fields.name: localMode
fields.doc: Compute the decal using the local mesh coordinates instead of world space. Useful when the source mesh is transformed.

fields.name: zOffset
fields.doc: Depth bias used to avoid z-fighting between the decal and the surface. Negative values push the decal towards the camera.

members.summary: Creates a geometry decal that projects an image onto a mesh.
members.doc:
Creates a geometry decal that projects an image onto a mesh. The decal is a clipped child mesh that hugs the
surface of the source mesh, which makes it work with any material and on any static mesh. It adds geometry, so
for deforming meshes or many accumulating decals prefer the decal map approach instead.

fields.doc: Width in pixels of the internal decal map render target.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Height in pixels of the internal decal map render target.

members.summary: Enables a UV-space decal map on a mesh and turns on the decal map plugin of its material.
members.doc:
Enables a UV-space decal map on a mesh and turns on the decal map plugin of its material. Unlike geometry decals
this projects images directly into the mesh texture space, so no geometry is added, decals follow deformation and
multiple projections accumulate into a single map. The mesh must have proper, non-overlapping UV coordinates.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: Projection direction in world coordinates, usually the surface normal at the projection point.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Size of the projection box on each axis.

fields.name: angle
fields.doc: Angle to rotate the projection around the projection direction, in radians.

members.doc:
Projects an image into a decal map. Each call adds the image at the given location, accumulating onto previously
projected decals. Use it together with a decal map enabled on the mesh.

members.doc:
The in-scene 2D interface: buttons, sliders, checkboxes, color pickers, text blocks, input
fields, images and the containers that lay them out. Use it for controls that live inside the 3D
canvas - a slider floating next to the model - rather than in the surrounding page.

members.name: advancedDynamicTexture
members.summary: The surface GUI controls are drawn on: a full-screen layer over the canvas, or a texture wrapped onto a mesh so the controls sit in the 3D scene.
members.doc:
The surface GUI controls are drawn on: a full-screen layer over the canvas, or a texture wrapped
onto a mesh so the controls sit in the 3D scene. Every control has to be added to one of these,
directly or through a container, before it shows.

members.name: createForMesh

fields.name: mesh
fields.doc:
The mesh the GUI is drawn on; it needs texture coordinates, a plane being the usual
choice

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Width of the GUI texture in pixels; left out, the engine chooses

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Height of the GUI texture in pixels; left out, the engine chooses

fields.name: supportPointerMove
fields.doc: When true, controls on the mesh react to the pointer moving over them, at some extra cost

fields.name: onlyAlphaTesting
fields.doc:
When true, transparent pixels are cut out instead of blended, which avoids sorting
problems

fields.name: invertY
fields.doc: When true, the texture is flipped top to bottom; the default is right for most meshes

fields.name: sampling
fields.doc:
How texture pixels are read when scaled: nearest keeps hard pixels, bilinear and
trilinear blend them

members.summary: Creates a GUI texture wrapped onto a mesh, so controls added to it appear on the mesh's surface in the scene; the mesh needs texture coordinates, a plane being the usual choice.
members.doc:
Creates a GUI texture wrapped onto a mesh, so controls added to it appear on the mesh's
surface in the scene; the mesh needs texture coordinates, a plane being the usual choice.

`width` and `height` size the texture in pixels, `supportPointerMove` lets controls react to
hover, and `onlyAlphaTesting` draws it without blending.

When true, the layer scales with the screen's pixel density so controls keep their size
on dense displays

members.summary: Creates the full-screen layer that GUI controls are added to, drawn over the whole canvas in front of the scene when `foreground` is true; `adaptiveScaling` scales the layer with the screen's pixel density.

members.name: meshBuilder
members.summary: BabylonJS's own mesh primitives, built straight into the scene as ready-to-render meshes rather than through a CAD kernel: boxes, spheres, discs, tori, polygons, tubes, polyhedra, capsules, cylinders, extrusions, ribbons, lathes and grounds.
members.doc:
BabylonJS's own mesh primitives, built straight into the scene as ready-to-render meshes rather
than through a CAD kernel: boxes, spheres, discs, tori, polygons, tubes, polyhedra, capsules,
cylinders, extrusions, ribbons, lathes and grounds. They are quick to make and cheap to draw but
carry no exact geometry, so use the kernels when the shape must be measured, cut or exported.
Every builder centers its mesh on the origin, sets `sideOrientation` and registers it for shadows
unless `enableShadows` is false.

the rotation, and the move back. Angles are in degrees. The `transforms` service on the base
package builds the same matrices without the engine.

members.doc:
Reading and writing CSV, the plain-text table format with one row per line and a separator
between cells. The parsers split on `rowSeparator` and `columnSeparator`, honor double-quoted
cells with doubled quotes inside, skip blank lines and read `\n`, `\t` and `\r` written as two
characters as the real thing; the writers quote a cell that contains a separator, a quote or a
line break.

members.name: draw
members.summary: Drawing anything into the scene: kernel shapes, points, lines, polylines, frames, curves, meshes and tags all go through `drawAnyAsync`, which picks the right renderer for the entity and returns the drawn object.
members.doc:
Drawing anything into the scene: kernel shapes, points, lines, polylines, frames, curves, meshes
and tags all go through `drawAnyAsync`, which picks the right renderer for the entity and returns
the drawn object. The `options` methods build the drawing options with defaults for each kind of
entity, `createPBRMaterial` and `createTexture` make materials for the face slots, and a drawn
object can be redrawn in place by passing it back.

members.name: detectNode
members.summary: Whether the entity is a node this renderer can draw an axis triad for.
members.doc:
Whether the entity is a node this renderer can draw an axis triad for.

The engine-agnostic check this replaces asks whether `id` is a string containing "node", which
any object can satisfy and most real nodes do not: it matched only the ones this library named
itself, so a node from a loaded model, or one a script constructed, typechecked as drawable
and then silently drew nothing. A node is a renderer's own concept, so the honest check lives
beside the renderer that has the type to ask about.

members.summary: Transform nodes: invisible points with a position and an orientation that meshes and other nodes can be parented to, so a whole group moves as one.
members.doc:
Transform nodes: invisible points with a position and an orientation that meshes and other nodes
can be parented to, so a whole group moves as one. Building a hierarchy of nodes is how complex
arrangements are placed: turn the parent and every child turns with it. The methods here create
nodes, read their axes and positions in world or local space, and move, rotate and reparent them;
angles are in degrees.

found.

Frames: a frame is a point with three axes at right angles, written as its `origin`, its `normal`
(the Z axis) and its `direction` (the X axis), the Y axis following from those two. Frames place
things: a shape lands on one, points convert between one and the world, and frame patterns lay
out copies. Every method returns new values and never changes its inputs.

along their widest spread, toward the first point; with no widest spread, as around a square,
X points at the first point. Fewer than three points, or nearly collinear ones, throw.

members.name: jscad
members.summary: The entry point to the JSCAD kernel, a mesh-based solid modeler with three kinds of geometry: a solid, held as a closed set of polygons; a flat 2D shape, held as a region in the XY plane; and a 2D path, an open or closed polyline in that plane.
members.doc:
The entry point to the JSCAD kernel, a mesh-based solid modeler with three kinds of geometry: a
solid, held as a closed set of polygons; a flat 2D shape, held as a region in the XY plane; and a
2D path, an open or closed polyline in that plane. `shapes` and `polygon` build them, `booleans`,
`extrusions`, `expansions` and `hulls` combine and grow them, `text` writes with them and
`colors` tints them. Flat shapes live in the XY plane and extrude along Z. The methods on the
service itself convert solids to mesh data, move them with matrices and write STL, DXF and 3MF
files. Credit to the JSCAD community for the kernel.

gives new geometry and leaves the inputs as they are.

members.summary: Growing and shrinking JSCAD geometry by a distance: `expand` moves every boundary outward, or inward for a negative distance, and `offset` builds the outline at that distance.
members.doc:
Growing and shrinking JSCAD geometry by a distance: `expand` moves every boundary outward, or
inward for a negative distance, and `offset` builds the outline at that distance. Both work on
flat 2D shapes and paths and shape their corners as `corners` says; `expand` also grows solids,
with round corners only.

members.name: expand

fields.name: geometry
fields.doc: The 2D shape, path or solid to grow; it stays as it is and a new entity comes back

fields.name: delta
fields.doc:
How far the boundary moves, in model units: positive grows the geometry, negative shrinks it;
a solid or a path accepts a positive value only

fields.name: corners
fields.doc:
How a convex corner is shaped: `round` curves it with `segments` pieces, `chamfer` cuts it
flat, `edge` keeps it sharp; a solid accepts `round` only

fields.name: segments
fields.doc:
Number of straight pieces a `round` corner is made of over a full circle; more makes it
smoother, and a solid needs at least 4

members.summary: Grows geometry by moving its whole boundary outward by `delta`, or shrinks it when `delta` is negative.
members.doc:
Grows geometry by moving its whole boundary outward by `delta`, or shrinks it when `delta` is
negative.

A 2D shape stays a 2D shape, a path becomes a 2D band of that width around it, and a solid
grows into a bigger solid, with round corners and a positive `delta` only. Corners are
rounded when `corners` is left out.

fields.doc: How far the boundary moves, in model units: positive grows the geometry, negative shrinks it

fields.doc:
How a convex corner is shaped: `edge` keeps it sharp, `chamfer` cuts it flat, `round` curves
it with `segments` pieces

fields.name: segments

Number of straight pieces a `round` corner is made of over a full circle; more makes it
smoother

members.doc:
Builds the outline of a 2D shape or path at distance `delta` from the original, outward for
positive and inward for negative.

A 2D shape gives a bigger or smaller 2D shape and a path gives a parallel path. When
`corners` is left out, corners are kept sharp.

members.name: extrusions

members.doc:
Turning flat JSCAD shapes into solids: straight extrusion along Z with an optional twist, a wall
built along an outline, and revolution around the Z axis. Every flat shape lies in the XY plane,
so the result grows out of that plane along Z.

when `twistAngle` is not zero.

number of slices used for it, at least 1. A negative `height` extrudes downward.

each side and raised by `height` along Z.

wraps everything at once and `hullChain` wraps each consecutive pair, so a row of shapes becomes

shapes or paths.

members.summary: Writing text with JSCAD's built-in stroke font.
members.doc:
Writing text with JSCAD's built-in stroke font. `createVectorText` gives the pen strokes of the
text as lists of 2D points in the XY plane; `cylindricalText` and `sphericalText` turn every
stroke into a solid by chaining hulled cylinders or spheres along it, centered on the origin. The
text `height` is the height of a capital letter in model units.

properties and preview data through the application; every change comes back as a changed copy,
the input stays as it is.

extend without end. Parallel lines, lines that pass each other without meeting, and segments

members.name: manifold
members.summary: The entry point to the Manifold kernel, a fast mesh-based solid modeler: `manifold` builds and changes solids, `crossSection` handles the flat outlines they are extruded and revolved from, and `mesh` reads the triangle data.
members.doc:
The entry point to the Manifold kernel, a fast mesh-based solid modeler: `manifold` builds and
changes solids, `crossSection` handles the flat outlines they are extruded and revolved from, and
`mesh` reads the triangle data. Manifold works on triangle meshes rather than exact curves, so
booleans are quick and always watertight, and it keeps its own Z axis as up: extrusions grow
along Z and slices are parallel to the XY plane. The methods on the service itself turn solids
and cross-sections into plain mesh data for drawing.

members.name: crossSection
members.summary: Flat outlines in the Manifold kernel, the 2D shapes that `operations.extrude` and `operations.revolve` turn into solids and that `slice` and `project` cut out of them.
members.doc:
Flat outlines in the Manifold kernel, the 2D shapes that `operations.extrude` and
`operations.revolve` turn into solids and that `slice` and `project` cut out of them. A
cross-section is one or more closed polygons in the XY plane, holes included; `shapes` builds
them, `booleans` combines them, `operations` offsets, hulls and extrudes them, `transforms` moves
them and `evaluate` measures them. The methods here convert between cross-sections and plain
point lists, and free the memory a cross-section holds.

members.name: manifold
members.summary: Solids in the Manifold kernel: `shapes` builds cubes, spheres, cylinders and solids from meshes, `booleans` fuses, cuts and splits them, `operations` hulls, slices, refines and smooths them, `transforms` moves them and `evaluate` measures them.

Solids in the Manifold kernel: `shapes` builds cubes, spheres, cylinders and solids from meshes,
`booleans` fuses, cuts and splits them, `operations` hulls, slices, refines and smooths them,
`transforms` moves them and `evaluate` measures them. A solid here is a closed triangle mesh;
every operation returns a new solid and the inputs stay as they are. The methods on this class
turn solids into plain mesh data.

solid with another solid or a plane. Because the kernel works on closed triangle meshes, these
are fast and always give a watertight result; the two-shape and many-shape forms give the same
results and exist for convenience. Every method returns new solids and leaves the inputs as they
are.

members.name: mesh
members.summary: Geometry on plain triangle meshes: a mesh is a list of triangles, each three points.
members.doc:
Geometry on plain triangle meshes: a mesh is a list of triangles, each three points. The methods
here work out the plane of a triangle, the distance from a point to a plane, and where two meshes
cut through each other, as segments, as polylines or as point lists. They need no CAD kernel, so
they run on any triangulated data.

members.summary: Finds the plane a triangle lies in: its unit normal and its distance from the origin along that normal.
members.doc:
Finds the plane a triangle lies in: its unit normal and its distance from the origin along
that normal.

The normal follows the right-hand rule around the triangle's points. A triangle with no area,
whose points are on one line, has no plane and gives undefined.
Example: [[0,0,0], [1,0,0], [0,1,0]] -> { normal: [0,0,1], d: 0 }

members.name: occt
members.summary: The entry point to the OpenCascade kernel: every OCCT feature is reached through one of its properties.
members.doc:
The entry point to the OpenCascade kernel: every OCCT feature is reached through one of its
properties. `shapes` builds and reads vertices, edges, wires, faces, shells, solids and
compounds; `operations`, `booleans`, `fillets`, `transforms`, `corners`, `draft` and `features`
change shapes; `select` picks faces and edges by what they are and where they lie; `analysis`
answers questions about shapes with points and numbers; `geom` handles
curves and surfaces; `io` reads and writes STEP, IGES, STL and other files; `assembly`,
`dimensions`, `brepGraph`, `path` and `svg` cover documents, annotations, topology graphs,
machining paths and SVG. The methods on the service itself turn shapes into triangle meshes for
drawing.

members.name: analysis
members.summary: Questions asked of OpenCascade shapes, answered with points, numbers and index lists rather than new shapes.
members.doc:
Questions asked of OpenCascade shapes, answered with points, numbers and index lists rather than
new shapes. `curves` reads edges and wires, `surfaces` reads faces, `measure` measures boxes,
distances, angles and radii, and `clashes` finds shapes and faces that overlap or come too close.
The shapes themselves are left as they are.

members.name: clashes
members.summary: Finding shapes and faces that overlap or come closer than a clearance: pairs among a list of placed shapes, faces of two shapes within a distance of each other, and faces of one shape that cut through each other.
members.doc:
Finding shapes and faces that overlap or come closer than a clearance: pairs among a list of
placed shapes, faces of two shapes within a distance of each other, and faces of one shape that
cut through each other. Each clash names the two items by index with the distance between them
and, for solids, the volume they share.

members.name: betweenShapes

fields.name: shapes
fields.doc: The shapes to check against each other; a clash names two of them by their positions here.

fields.name: clearance
fields.doc:
How close two shapes may come before they clash, in model units; 0 reports only shapes that
touch or overlap.

members.summary: Finds every pair among a list of shapes that overlap, touch or come within a clearance of each other, such as colliding parts.
members.doc:
Finds every pair among a list of shapes that overlap, touch or come within a clearance of each
other, such as colliding parts.

A clash names the two by their positions in the list, from 0, with their distance, 0 where they
touch, overlap or nest, and the volume two solids share.

members.name: facesWithin

fields.name: shapeA
fields.doc: The first shape, whose faces are side A of each clash.

fields.name: shapeB
fields.doc: The second shape, whose faces are side B of each clash.

fields.name: clearance
fields.doc:
How close a face of one shape may come to a face of the other before the two clash, in model
units.

fields.name: precision
fields.doc:
The mesh deflection of the search for candidate pairs, in model units; every pair it finds is
then measured exactly.

members.summary: Finds the faces of one shape that come within a clearance of faces of another, each pair measured exactly.
members.doc:
Finds the faces of one shape that come within a clearance of faces of another, each pair
measured exactly.

A clash names a face of each as `shapes.face.getFaces` numbers them, sorted by the first shape's
face. Candidates come from meshes of copies at `precision`, so the shapes given stay unmeshed;
faces without a surface take no part.

members.name: selfIntersections

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape whose faces are checked against each other.

fields.name: precision
fields.doc:
The mesh deflection of the search for candidate pairs, in model units; every pair it finds is
then confirmed exactly.

members.summary: Finds the pairs of faces of one shape that cross each other anywhere but along an edge they share.
members.doc:
Finds the pairs of faces of one shape that cross each other anywhere but along an edge they
share.

A clash names the two faces as `shapes.face.getFaces` numbers them, with both points at one
place on their crossing. Candidates come from a mesh of a copy at `precision` and are confirmed
exactly; a mere touch can be missed.

members.name: curves
members.summary: Questions asked of edges and wires, answered with points and numbers rather than new shapes: the closest point with its parameter and length along the curve, curvature and its comb, kinks where the tangent turns, extremes along a direction, and intersections with other curves and with faces.
members.doc:
Questions asked of edges and wires, answered with points and numbers rather than new shapes: the
closest point with its parameter and length along the curve, curvature and its comb, kinks where
the tangent turns, extremes along a direction, and intersections with other curves and with faces.
Parameters are fractions from 0 at the start to 1 at the end, where each edge of a wire takes an
equal share, as `shapes.wire.pointOnWireAtParam` takes them. Edges are numbered as
`shapes.edge.getEdgesAlongWire` lists them, and angles are in degrees.

members.name: closestPoints

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape the closest points are looked for on.

fields.name: points
fields.doc: The points to measure from, in the order the results should come back.

members.summary: Finds the point of an edge or a wire nearest each given point, with where it lies along the curve.
members.doc:
Finds the point of an edge or a wire nearest each given point, with where it lies along the
curve.

Each result carries the point, its parameter as a fraction of the curve, its length from the
start, its distance from the given point and the edge it lies on; at a corner that is the
edge starting there.

members.name: curvatureComb

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The edge or wire whose curvature is drawn.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: How many teeth, spaced evenly by length from the start of the curve to its end.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc:
How long a tooth is per unit of curvature; 0 picks the scale that makes the longest tooth a
fifth of the curve's length.

members.summary: Draws a curvature comb along an edge or a wire: teeth standing on the curve, as long as the curvature there, pointing away from its center.
members.doc:
Draws a curvature comb along an edge or a wire: teeth standing on the curve, as long as the
curvature there, pointing away from its center.

The first polyline runs through the tips, showing how the curvature changes; then comes one
two-point polyline per tooth, from the curve to its tip. The teeth are spaced evenly by length.

members.name: curvaturesAtLengths

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The edge or wire to evaluate; each method says which it takes.

fields.name: lengths
fields.doc: The distances from the start along the wire, in model units, one point each.

members.summary: Reads how an edge or a wire bends at places given as lengths along it from its start, in model units.
members.doc:
Reads how an edge or a wire bends at places given as lengths along it from its start, in model
units.

Each result is what `curvaturesAtParams` gives: the point, the tangent, normal and binormal,
the curvature with its radius and center, and the torsion. At a corner of a wire the edge
starting there is read.

members.name: curvaturesAtParams

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The edge or wire to read or cut.

fields.name: params
fields.doc:
Places along the curve, each a fraction from 0 at the start to 1 at the end; each edge of a
wire takes an equal share, as in `shapes.wire.pointOnWireAtParam`.

members.summary: Reads how an edge or a wire bends at places given as fractions from 0 at its start to 1 at its end.
members.doc:
Reads how an edge or a wire bends at places given as fractions from 0 at its start to 1 at its
end.

Each result holds the point, tangent, normal, binormal, curvature, radius, center and torsion;
a straight stretch reads `isStraight` with an `Infinity` radius. At a corner of a wire the edge
starting there is read.

members.name: curveType

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape to work on; it is not changed.

members.summary: Tells what kind of curve an edge runs along: a line, a circle, an ellipse, a hyperbola, a parabola, a Bezier curve, a B-spline, an offset curve or another kind.
members.doc:
Tells what kind of curve an edge runs along: a line, a circle, an ellipse, a hyperbola, a
parabola, a Bezier curve, a B-spline, an offset curve or another kind.

The kinds are the ones `select.edges.ofType` chooses edges by.

members.name: extremesAlong

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The edge or wire to look along.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc: The way up: the highest points lie furthest along it; only its direction matters.

members.summary: Finds the highest and lowest points of an edge or a wire along a direction, such as the crests of a wave.
members.doc:
Finds the highest and lowest points of an edge or a wire along a direction, such as the crests
of a wave.

They come in order along the curve, marked as maxima or minima, and as global when nothing lies
higher, or lower; ties are all global. An open curve's ends count; a level stretch is reported
at its start.

members.name: intersectCurveWithFace

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The edge or wire that meets the face; the points come back in order along it.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: The face the curve meets, within its edges; the surface beyond them does not count.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.doc:
How close the curve may pass and still count as meeting the face, in model units; points
closer than it to each other merge into one.

members.summary: Finds where an edge or a wire passes through a face or lies on it, within the face's edges.
members.doc:
Finds where an edge or a wire passes through a face or lies on it, within the face's edges.

The points come in order along the curve, with `u` and `v` as the fractions that
`shapes.face.pointOnUV` takes. A stretch lying on the face gives its two ends, marked
`isOverlap`.

members.name: intersectCurves

fields.name: shapeA
fields.doc: The first edge or wire; the points come back in order along it.

fields.name: shapeB
fields.doc: The second edge or wire, the one the first meets.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.doc:
How close the curves may pass and still count as meeting, in model units; points closer than
it to each other merge into one.

members.summary: Finds where two edges or wires cross or touch, with the parameter and the edge of each point on both curves.
members.doc:
Finds where two edges or wires cross or touch, with the parameter and the edge of each point on
both curves.

The points come in order along the first curve. Where the curves run together, the two ends of
the shared stretch come back marked `isOverlap`; curves that do not meet give an empty list.

members.name: kinks

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The edge or wire to look along.

fields.name: angle
fields.doc:
How far the tangent must turn where two edges meet for the joint to count as a kink, in
degrees; a turn of exactly this much does not count.

members.summary: Finds the corners of an edge or a wire where the tangent turns by more than an angle, such as the corners of a polyline.
members.doc:
Finds the corners of an edge or a wire where the tangent turns by more than an angle, such as
the corners of a polyline.

Each kink comes with the edge ending there and the turn in degrees, in walking order; a closed
wire's closing corner, at its start, comes first.

members.name: measure
members.summary: Measurements of shapes: a bounding box that follows the geometry exactly, a box in a frame, the box turned to fit and the principal axes of inertia, every closest pair of points between two shapes with the sub-shapes they lie on, angles between faces and edges, the dihedral angle along an edge, and the tightest radius of curvature.
members.doc:
Measurements of shapes: a bounding box that follows the geometry exactly, a box in a frame, the
box turned to fit and the principal axes of inertia, every closest pair of points between two
shapes with the sub-shapes they lie on, angles between faces and edges, the dihedral angle along an
edge, and the tightest radius of curvature. Lengths are in model units and angles in degrees.

members.name: angleBetween

fields.name: shapeA
fields.doc: The first shape, side A of the results.

fields.name: shapeB
fields.doc: The second shape, side B of the results.

members.summary: Measures the angle in degrees between two faces or edges where they come nearest each other.
members.doc:
Measures the angle in degrees between two faces or edges where they come nearest each other.

Faces compare their normals, 0 when they look the same way and 180 when opposite; edges compare
their tangents; a face and an edge compare the normal with the tangent, so the edge meets the
face's plane at 90 minus the angle.

members.name: boundingBoxInFrame

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape the box is found around.

fields.name: frame
fields.doc:
The frame whose axes the box follows: its x along the frame's direction and its z along the
frame's normal. Only the axes matter, not the origin.

members.summary: Finds the box that just holds a shape with its sides along a frame's axes instead of the world's.
members.doc:
Finds the box that just holds a shape with its sides along a frame's axes instead of the
world's.

The box's x runs along the frame's direction and its z along the normal. It comes back as a
frame at its center and half its size along each axis; `orientedBoundingBox` turns the box to
fit instead.

members.name: dihedralAngle

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape the edge belongs to.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: The edge, counted from 0 as `shapes.edge.getEdges` lists them.

fields.name: param
fields.doc:
Where along the edge the angle is read, as a share of its parameter range from 0 at its start
to 1 at its end.

members.summary: Measures the angle through the material between the two faces that meet at an edge.
members.doc:
Measures the angle through the material between the two faces that meet at an edge.

A box's edges read 90 degrees, a smooth join 180 and an L's inner edge 270; up to 180 the edge
is convex. `param` is a share of the edge's parameter range, and of its length only on lines and
circles.

members.name: extrema

fields.name: shapeA
fields.doc: The first shape, side A of the results.

fields.name: shapeB
fields.doc: The second shape, side B of the results.

members.summary: Finds every nearest pair of points between two shapes, with the vertex, edge or face each point lies on and where on it.
members.doc:
Finds every nearest pair of points between two shapes, with the vertex, edge or face each point
lies on and where on it.

Touching, overlapping and nested shapes are 0 apart; a shape inside another gives one pair on
one of its vertices, with -1 as the containing side's index.
`operations.closestPointsBetweenTwoShapes` gives one pair alone.

members.name: minCurvatureRadius

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape whose tightest bend is found.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc:
How densely the shape is read: a grid of this many by this many places on each face, and this
many places along each edge.

fields.name: concaveOnly
fields.doc:
True reads only where faces bend concavely, the tightest radius a round tool can reach; edges
and convex bends are then skipped.

members.summary: Finds the tightest bend of a shape, sampled over its faces and edges, and where it is.
members.doc:
Finds the tightest bend of a shape, sampled over its faces and edges, and where it is.

Each face is read on a grid of `samples` by `samples` places inside its trims and each edge at
`samples` places, so a tighter bend between them can be missed. A sharp edge between faces is no
bend; `dihedralAngle` measures it.

members.name: orientedBoundingBox

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape to work on; it is not changed.

members.summary: Finds the smallest box that fits around a shape, turned to follow it rather than the axes: a frame at the box's centre, its direction along the longest side and its normal along the shortest, with half the box's size along each.
members.doc:
Finds the smallest box that fits around a shape, turned to follow it rather than the axes: a
frame at the box's centre, its direction along the longest side and its normal along the
shortest, with half the box's size along each.

`boundingBoxInFrame` keeps the axes of a frame you give instead.

members.name: principalFrame

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape to work on; it is not changed.

members.summary: Finds a shape's principal axes of inertia as a frame at its centre of mass: the direction is the axis it turns about most easily, the normal the one it resists most.
members.doc:
Finds a shape's principal axes of inertia as a frame at its centre of mass: the direction is
the axis it turns about most easily, the normal the one it resists most.

Solids are measured by volume, even inside out, else faces by area, else edges by length, at
a density of 1. Each axis's largest coordinate is positive.

Finds the box lined up with the axes that just holds a shape's exact geometry.

Unlike `operations.boundingBoxOfShape`, which may add tolerances and the mesh, it leaves no gap:
a ball of radius 3 gets a box of 6. A face carrying only a mesh is boxed by its nodes; a shape
with nothing to bound is refused.

members.doc:
Questions asked of faces, answered with points and numbers: the closest point with its (u, v), the
principal, mean and Gaussian curvature at (u, v) values, and the kind of surface a face lies on.
(u, v) values are fractions of the face's UV bounds, from 0 at the start to 1 at the end, the
values `shapes.face.pointOnUV` and the other face samplers take.

members.doc:
Finds the point of a face nearest each given point, with its (u, v) and the face's normal there.

The face is bounded, so a point beyond its edges comes to its boundary, which `isOnBoundary`
says. `u` and `v` are fractions of the face's UV bounds, as `shapes.face.pointOnUV` takes them;
`operations.closestPointsOnShapeFromPoints` gives the points alone, for any shape.

members.doc:
Reads how a face bends at (u, v) pairs: its largest and smallest curvature with their
directions, their mean and product, and the normal.

U and V are fractions of the face's UV bounds. A curvature is 1 over a radius, positive where the
face bulges out along its normal, so the inside of a hole reads negative.

members.doc:
Tells what kind of surface a face lies on, such as a plane, a cylinder or a B-spline.

A surface trimmed to a rectangle reads as the surface it trims, as `select.faces.ofType` reads
it, and a face without a surface, as an imported mesh has, reads as `other`. A shape that is not
a face is refused.

members.name: assembly
members.summary: Assemblies as OpenCascade documents: a document holds parts, the sub-assemblies that group them and the instances that place them, with names, colors and placements, the way a STEP assembly does.
members.doc:
Assemblies as OpenCascade documents: a document holds parts, the sub-assemblies that group them
and the instances that place them, with names, colors and placements, the way a STEP assembly
does. `manager` builds documents step by step from parts and nodes, loads STEP, glTF and OBJ files
into them, changes labels and exports to STEP, glTF, OBJ and PLY; `query` reads parts, shapes,
colors, placements, the hierarchy and the dimensions and tolerances back out. Every label in a
document is addressed by its label id string. A document stays in memory until it is deleted.

members.name: manager
members.summary: Building and changing assembly documents: describe parts, assembly nodes and instance nodes one object at a time, combine them into a structure, and build a document from it; or load a STEP, glTF or OBJ file into a document.
members.doc:
Building and changing assembly documents: describe parts, assembly nodes and instance nodes one
object at a time, combine them into a structure, and build a document from it; or load a STEP,
glTF or OBJ file into a document. Then recolor and rename labels, update or remove parts, and
export to STEP, glTF, OBJ or PLY. A document is an in-memory handle that stays alive until it is
deleted, so build once and query or export as often as needed.

are applied first, then the new parts and nodes added.

members.doc:
Builds an assembly document from a structure, or applies the structure to an existing
document.

With `existingDocument` the labels in `removals` are dropped first, the `partUpdates`
applied, then the new parts and nodes added; a structure with neither clears the document
unless `clearDocument` is false. `sourceDocuments` supplies the documents imported parts copy
from. The document stays in memory until deleted.

structure definition, the last step before `buildAssemblyDocument`.

`clearDocument` false keeps what an existing document already holds when the structure is
applied to it.

Describes an instance node, one placement of a part: which part by `partId`, where it goes
and under which assembly.

`translation` moves it, `rotation` turns it by Euler angles in degrees about X, Y and Z,
`scale` sizes it uniformly; a `matrix` can replace all three. The same part may be placed by
many instances.

fields.doc: How closely triangles follow curved surfaces, in model units; smaller gives a finer mesh.

fields.doc:
The largest angle, in radians, between the normals of neighboring triangles; smaller gives
smoother curves.

When true, extra vertices are added inside curved faces for a closer fit, at the cost of
speed.

When true, an extra pass refines triangles that bulge beyond the deflection, at the cost of
speed.

separate.

names and colors kept as glTF nodes and materials.

When true, extra vertices are added inside curved faces for a closer fit, at the cost of

from another, intersection keeps only what they share. These work on the exact geometry and give
exact results. The mesh intersection methods instead triangulate the shapes and intersect the
triangles, which is faster and more robust on awkward geometry but gives polylines rather than
curves. Every method returns a new shape; unless `keepEdges` is set, faces that end up lying on
one surface are merged and the seams between them removed.

members.doc:
Draft angles for OpenCascade shapes: the slight taper cast and molded parts need so they slide
out of the mold. `draftAngle` tilts chosen faces of a solid about a neutral plane, while
`makeDraft` and `makeDraftToShape` grow a tapered skirt from a wire or the edges of a shape along
a pull direction. Angles are in degrees.

Tilts the selected faces of a shape by a draft angle so the part can be pulled out of a mold
along `direction`.

The faces pivot about the neutral plane, given by a point and a normal, which stays put;
`angle` is in degrees. `flag` keeps the standard draft side, false tapers the other way.
Undraftable faces throw.

sketched on a face, tapered and revolved ones, ribs and grooves from a wire, and faces removed or

base, such as `operations.sweepEvolved`, live in `operations`.

rounded surface of a given radius, a chamfer with a flat bevel of a given distance. Edges are
chosen by 0-based index in the order `shapes.edge.getEdges` lists them, or passed in directly;
flat outlines and faces are rounded at their corners with `fillet2d`, whose corner indexes
start at 1. A radius that does not fit, for instance larger than a neighbouring face, makes
the kernel fail, so start small. Every method returns a new shape.

members.name: geom
members.summary: The geometric layer beneath the topology: the mathematical curves and surfaces themselves, separate from the edges and faces that carry them.
members.doc:
The geometric layer beneath the topology: the mathematical curves and surfaces themselves,
separate from the edges and faces that carry them. `curves` builds 2D curves for constructions in
UV space and evaluates them; `surfaces` builds infinite surfaces and extracts the surface a face
lies on. These objects cannot be drawn directly: wrap them into edges and faces with
`shapes.edge` and `shapes.face` first.

members.name: curves
members.summary: Construction curves of OpenCascade: 2D curves in a plane or in the UV space of a surface (circles, ellipses, segments, trimmed pieces), which feed `shapes.edge.makeEdgeFromGeom2dCurveAndSurface`, and circle and ellipse wires.
members.doc:
Construction curves of OpenCascade: 2D curves in a plane or in the UV space of a surface
(circles, ellipses, segments, trimmed pieces), which feed
`shapes.edge.makeEdgeFromGeom2dCurveAndSurface`, and circle and ellipse wires. The 2D curves have
no topology and cannot be drawn; a point on them is read with `get2dPointFrom2dCurveOnParam`.

Creates a 2D ellipse curve in a plane, for constructions in the UV space of a surface.

`direction` is the direction of the major axis; `radiusMajor` must be at least `radiusMinor`,
and `sense` flips the curve's direction. The curve cannot be drawn; wrap it with
`shapes.edge.makeEdgeFromGeom2dCurveAndSurface`.

Construction surfaces of OpenCascade: the infinite mathematical surfaces that faces are cut from.
`cylindricalSurface` builds one and `surfaceFromFace` reads the surface a face lies on; both feed
`shapes.face.faceFromSurface`, `shapes.face.faceFromSurfaceAndWire` and
`shapes.edge.makeEdgeFromGeom2dCurveAndSurface`. A surface has no boundary and cannot be drawn by
itself.

after making a face.

Reads the underlying surface a face lies on, without its boundary.

A face is a bounded piece of such a surface; the surface itself extends beyond the face,
which is what lets a new wire be placed on it and cut into a different face.

members.doc:
Reading and writing CAD files with OCCT: everything `io` offers on the kernel, plus loaders that
take a STEP or IGES file as a File object or as its text and give back a shape. Files are Z-up by
convention, so `adjustZtoY` turns the loaded shape to this library's Y-up unless it is set false.

members.name: convertStepToGltf

fields.name: stepData
fields.doc:
The STEP file as text, ArrayBuffer, Uint8Array, File or Blob; gzip-compressed `.stpz` content
is unpacked on its own.

fields.name: meshPrecision
fields.doc:
How closely triangles follow curved surfaces: with `meshRelative` true a fraction of each
edge's length, otherwise an absolute distance in model units.

fields.name: meshAngle
fields.doc:
The largest angle, in radians, between the normals of neighboring triangles; smaller gives
smoother curves and more triangles.

fields.name: meshRelative
fields.doc:
When true, `meshPrecision` scales with each part's size, so small fasteners and large
housings both mesh well; when false it is an absolute distance.

fields.name: internalVerticesMode
fields.doc:
When true, extra vertices are added inside curved faces for a closer fit, at the cost of
speed.

fields.name: controlSurfaceDeflection
fields.doc:
When true, an extra pass refines triangles that bulge beyond the precision, at the cost of
speed.

members.summary: Converts a STEP file into a binary glTF (GLB), keeping the assembly tree as glTF nodes along with part names, colors, materials and placements.
members.doc:
Converts a STEP file into a binary glTF (GLB), keeping the assembly tree as glTF nodes along
with part names, colors, materials and placements.

`stepData` is the file as text, ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array. The mesh settings say how finely
curved surfaces are triangulated: `meshPrecision` is the deflection, `meshAngle` the angular
deflection. Z-up becomes glTF's Y-up. Failure throws.

members.name: convertStepToGltfAdvanced

fields.name: stepData
fields.doc:
The STEP file as text, ArrayBuffer, Uint8Array, File or Blob; gzip-compressed `.stpz` content
is unpacked on its own.

fields.name: readColors
fields.doc: When true, colors are read from the file; needed for a colored glTF.

fields.name: readNames
fields.doc:
When true, part names are read from the file; switch it off for faster parsing when names are
not needed.

fields.name: readMaterials
fields.doc: When true, materials are read from the file; needed for material properties in the glTF.

fields.name: readLayers
fields.doc: When true, layer information is read from the file; rarely needed for glTF.

fields.name: readProps
fields.doc: When true, validation properties are read from the file; rarely needed for glTF.

fields.name: meshDeflection
fields.doc:
How closely triangles follow curved surfaces: with `meshRelative` true a fraction of each
edge's length, otherwise an absolute distance in model units.

fields.name: meshAngle
fields.doc:
The largest angle, in radians, between the normals of neighboring triangles; smaller gives
smoother curves and more triangles.

fields.name: meshParallel
fields.doc: When true, faces are meshed on several threads where the build allows it.

fields.name: faceCountThreshold
fields.doc:
Above this many faces the assembly is meshed solid by solid to save memory; -1 meshes
everything in one pass, which is fastest.

fields.name: meshRelative
fields.doc:
When true, `meshDeflection` scales with each part's size, so small fasteners and large
housings both mesh well; when false it is an absolute distance.

fields.name: internalVerticesMode
fields.doc:
When true, extra vertices are added inside curved faces for a closer fit, at the cost of
speed.

fields.name: controlSurfaceDeflection
fields.doc:
When true, an extra pass refines triangles that bulge beyond the precision, at the cost of
speed.

fields.name: mergeFaces
fields.doc: When true, the faces of a part are joined into one mesh, which makes a smaller file.

fields.name: splitIndices16
fields.doc: When true, merged meshes use 16-bit indexes where they fit, which makes a smaller file.

fields.name: parallelWrite
fields.doc: When true, the glTF is written on several threads, which helps with large files.

fields.name: embedTextures
fields.doc: When true, textures are embedded in the GLB instead of referenced as separate files.

fields.name: forceUVExport
fields.doc: When true, texture coordinates are written even for meshes without textures.

fields.name: nodeNameFormat
fields.doc: What the glTF nodes are named after: the instance, the product, a combination, or nothing.

fields.name: meshNameFormat
fields.doc: What the glTF meshes are named after: the instance, the product, a combination, or nothing.

fields.name: transformFormat
fields.doc:
How node placements are written: `compact` as translation, rotation and scale where possible,
`mat4` always as a matrix, `trs` always as the three parts.

exposed.

The read flags choose what to take from the file (colors, names, materials, layers,
properties), the mesh settings how finely to triangulate, the export settings how the glTF is
written (merged faces, 16-bit indexes, naming, scale). Switch off what you do not need.

fields.name: readColors
fields.doc: When true, colors are read from the file; needed for a colored glTF.

fields.name: readNames
fields.doc:
When true, part names are read from the file; switch it off for faster parsing when names are
not needed.

fields.name: readMaterials
fields.doc: When true, materials are read from the file; needed for material properties in the glTF.

fields.name: readLayers
fields.doc: When true, layer information is read from the file; rarely needed for glTF.

fields.name: readProps
fields.doc: When true, validation properties are read from the file; rarely needed for glTF.

fields.name: meshDeflection
fields.doc:
How closely triangles follow curved surfaces: with `meshRelative` true a fraction of each
edge's length, otherwise an absolute distance in model units.

fields.name: meshAngle
fields.doc:
The largest angle, in radians, between the normals of neighboring triangles; smaller gives
smoother curves and more triangles.

fields.name: meshParallel
fields.doc: When true, faces are meshed on several threads where the build allows it.

fields.name: faceCountThreshold
fields.doc:
Above this many faces the assembly is meshed solid by solid to save memory; -1 meshes
everything in one pass, which is fastest.

fields.name: meshRelative
fields.doc:
When true, `meshDeflection` scales with each part's size, so small fasteners and large
housings both mesh well; when false it is an absolute distance.

fields.name: internalVerticesMode
fields.doc:
When true, extra vertices are added inside curved faces for a closer fit, at the cost of
speed.

fields.name: controlSurfaceDeflection
fields.doc:
When true, an extra pass refines triangles that bulge beyond the precision, at the cost of
speed.

fields.name: mergeFaces
fields.doc: When true, the faces of a part are joined into one mesh, which makes a smaller file.

fields.name: splitIndices16
fields.doc: When true, merged meshes use 16-bit indexes where they fit, which makes a smaller file.

fields.name: parallelWrite
fields.doc: When true, the glTF is written on several threads, which helps with large files.

fields.name: embedTextures
fields.doc: When true, textures are embedded in the GLB instead of referenced as separate files.

fields.name: forceUVExport
fields.doc: When true, texture coordinates are written even for meshes without textures.

fields.name: nodeNameFormat
fields.doc: What the glTF nodes are named after: the instance, the product, a combination, or nothing.

fields.name: meshNameFormat
fields.doc: What the glTF meshes are named after: the instance, the product, a combination, or nothing.

fields.name: transformFormat
fields.doc:
How node placements are written: `compact` as translation, rotation and scale where possible,
`mat4` always as a matrix, `trs` always as the three parts.

fields.name: adjustZtoY
fields.doc: When true, the file's Z-up is turned into glTF's Y-up; false keeps Z up.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc:
A factor applied to the whole model, such as 0.001 to turn millimeters into meters; 1 keeps
the size.

fields.name: useDraco
fields.doc: When true, the geometry is compressed with Draco.

fields.name: dracoCompressionLevel
fields.doc: How hard Draco compresses, from 0 for fastest and largest to 10 for slowest and smallest.

fields.name: dracoQuantizePositionBits
fields.doc: How many bits each vertex position keeps; fewer bits mean a smaller file and less precision.

fields.name: dracoQuantizeNormalBits
fields.doc: How many bits each normal keeps; fewer bits mean a smaller file and less precision.

fields.name: dracoQuantizeTexcoordBits
fields.doc:
How many bits each texture coordinate keeps; fewer bits mean a smaller file and less
precision.

fields.name: dracoQuantizeColorBits
fields.doc: How many bits each vertex color keeps; fewer bits mean a smaller file and less precision.

fields.name: dracoQuantizeGenericBits
fields.doc:
How many bits other vertex attributes keep; fewer bits mean a smaller file and less
precision.

fields.name: dracoUnifiedQuantization
fields.doc: When true, one quantization grid is used for every attribute instead of one per attribute.

deflection settings say how closely curved edges are followed. Give the paths a layer with
`dxfPathsWithLayer` and write the file with `dxfCreate`.

members.name: operations
members.summary: The modeling operations that turn OpenCascade wires and faces into surfaces and solids and measure shapes: lofting through sections, extruding and revolving, sweeping profiles along paths, offsetting, thickening shells into solids, slicing, sectioning and splitting, and hidden-line drawings, plus bounding boxes, bounding spheres and closest-point queries, which move to `analysis.measure` in the next major version.
members.doc:
The modeling operations that turn OpenCascade wires and faces into surfaces and solids and
measure shapes: lofting through sections, extruding and revolving, sweeping profiles along paths,
offsetting, thickening shells into solids, slicing, sectioning and splitting, and hidden-line
drawings, plus bounding boxes, bounding spheres and closest-point queries, which move to
`analysis.measure` in the next major version. Distances are in model units and angles in degrees;
every operation returns a new shape. Booleans live in `booleans`, rounding in `fillets` and local
features such as holes in `features`.

members.doc:
Builds a surface through a series of wires, like skin stretched over ribs: each wire is one

Extrudes a flat shape up along Y by `height` while twisting it by `angle` degrees about the Y
axis, like a twisted column.

The shape should lie flat, as the profiles this package creates do. With `makeSolid` true,
the default, a face profile gives a closed solid; a wire gives a twisted shell.

members.summary: Finds the curves where two shapes meet and joins them end to end into wires, such as the outline a plane cuts from a solid.
members.doc:
Finds the curves where two shapes meet and joins them end to end into wires, such as the
outline a plane cuts from a solid.

A loop comes back as a closed wire, branches or loose ends as open wires, and shapes that do
not meet give an empty list.

members.name: slice

fields.doc: The solid, or shape holding solids, to slice.

fields.name: step
fields.doc: The distance between slices, in model units; must be above 0.

fields.doc: The direction the slices are stacked along; each cutting plane is perpendicular to it.

members.summary: Cuts a solid into parallel slices along a direction, like a loaf of bread, every `step` model units from the bottom of the shape up.
members.doc:
Cuts a solid into parallel slices along a direction, like a loaf of bread, every `step` model
units from the bottom of the shape up.

Each slice is the flat section where a cutting plane meets the solid, all in one compound. The
shape must contain solids, and a step giving more than 100000 slices is refused.

members.name: sliceByFrames

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape to slice: faces come from its solids, wires from its solids, shells and faces.

fields.name: frames
fields.doc:
One plane per frame, through the frame's origin and square to its normal; the frame's
direction does not matter.

fields.name: makeFaces
fields.doc:
When true, each slice holds the faces where its plane passes through the solids, holes
included; when false, it holds the section wires.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.doc: How close the ends of two section edges must lie to be joined into one wire, in model units.

members.summary: Slices a shape with the plane of each frame, which passes through the frame's origin square to its normal.
members.doc:
Slices a shape with the plane of each frame, which passes through the frame's origin square to
its normal.

With `makeFaces` true a slice holds the faces where the plane passes through the solids, holes
included; with false, the section wires. A plane that misses the shape gives an empty compound.

members.name: sliceInStepPattern

fields.name: shape

fields.name: direction
fields.doc: The direction the slices are stacked along; each cutting plane is perpendicular to it.

members.summary: Cuts a solid into parallel slices like `slice`, but with a repeating pattern of gaps between them, such as 0.1, 0.5, 0.1, 0.5.
members.doc:
Cuts a solid into parallel slices like `slice`, but with a repeating pattern of gaps between
them, such as 0.1, 0.5, 0.1, 0.5.

The pattern repeats from the bottom of the shape up to its top. Steps must add up to more than
0 and give at most 100000 slices.

members.name: splitByFrame

fields.doc:
The shape to split: its solids become the pieces, or its faces when it has no solids, or its
edges when it has neither.

fields.name: frame

The plane to split along, through the frame's origin; `front` holds what lies on the side its

members.summary: Splits a shape in two with the plane of a frame: what lies on the side the frame's normal points to comes back as `front`, the rest as `back`.
members.doc:
Splits a shape in two with the plane of a frame: what lies on the side the frame's normal
points to comes back as `front`, the rest as `back`.

The pieces are solids when the shape has any, else faces, else edges. A shape the plane misses
comes back whole on its side.

members.doc:
Cuts a face into pieces along edges or wires lying on it, like scoring a sheet.

A cutter cuts only where it lies on the face, and a closed loop inside it cuts out the region it
encloses. With no cutters the face comes back whole.

How far apart geometry may be and still count as touching, in model units; helps when faces

When true, the inputs stay untouched and the result holds the pieces of every shape involved;
when false only the pieces of `shape` come back.

members.summary: Cuts a shape into pieces with other shapes, the way a knife splits a loaf, without removing any material.
members.doc:
Cuts a shape into pieces with other shapes, the way a knife splits a loaf, without removing
any material.

With `nonDestructive` true, the default, the inputs are left untouched and the result holds
the pieces of every shape involved, the cutters included; with false only the pieces of
`shape` come back. `localFuzzyTolerance` lets geometry that nearly touches count as touching.

members.name: path
members.summary: A generic 2D path builder: describe an outline as subpaths of line, quadratic, cubic and arc segments, the vocabulary of SVG paths, and get an OpenCascade wire or face in one call.
members.doc:
A generic 2D path builder: describe an outline as subpaths of line, quadratic, cubic and arc
segments, the vocabulary of SVG paths, and get an OpenCascade wire or face in one call. It knows
nothing about SVG itself; the SVG importer in `svg` translates documents into this vocabulary and
calls it.

members.summary: Builds a shape from path subpaths: one wire per subpath, packed into a compound when there are several, or a face when `makeFaces` is true and the outlines close.
members.doc:
Builds a shape from path subpaths: one wire per subpath, packed into a compound when there
are several, or a face when `makeFaces` is true and the outlines close.

`joinSegments` merges consecutive segments into single edges within `tolerance`; `scale` and
`flipY` map the path's units and downward Y axis onto the ground plane. An empty path gives
undefined.

members.name: select
members.summary: Choosing faces and edges of OpenCascade shapes by what they are, where they lie and how they meet, rather than by an index that shifts whenever the model changes.
members.doc:
Choosing faces and edges of OpenCascade shapes by what they are, where they lie and how they
meet, rather than by an index that shifts whenever the model changes. `faces` and `edges` return
index lists in the getters' numbering, which fillets, chamfers and the getters take as they are,
and which the selectors narrow further through their `indexes` input. A choice of nothing stays
empty through the selectors, but `fillets.filletEdges` and `fillets.chamferEdges` read an empty
`indexes` as every edge, and hand out `radiusList` and `distanceList` in the getters' order.

members.name: edges
members.summary: Choosing the edges of an OpenCascade shape by what they are, where they lie and how they meet, so that "the edges round the top" still names the right edges after a parameter changes.
members.doc:
Choosing the edges of an OpenCascade shape by what they are, where they lie and how they meet,
so that "the edges round the top" still names the right edges after a parameter changes. Every
method returns edge indexes as `shapes.edge.getEdges` counts them, from 0, which `fillets`, the
getters and the other selectors take as they are. `indexes` limits a filter to edges chosen
before, keeping their order; left out, every edge is a candidate, and an empty list chooses
nothing. Degenerate edges, the poles of a sphere, are never chosen.

members.summary: Checks and repairs for OpenCascade shapes that came out of a file or an operation with defects: gaps between edges, edges too short to matter, faces turned the wrong way, shells left open, tolerances that drifted.
members.doc:
Checks and repairs for OpenCascade shapes that came out of a file or an operation with defects:
gaps between edges, edges too short to matter, faces turned the wrong way, shells left open,
tolerances that drifted. `isValid` tells whether a shape is well formed, `validityReport` says what
is wrong and where, and `freeBoundaries` shows the rims of openings; `basicShapeRepair` is the
general fix, the shell, solid and sewing fixes and the wire fixes handle the rest. Every repair
returns a new shape.

members.doc:
Runs the kernel's general repair over a shape: closes small gaps, fixes wire and face defects
and brings tolerances into the given range.

`precision` is the size of defect to look for, `minTolerance` and `maxTolerance` bound the
tolerances the repaired shape may carry, all in model units. Try it first on any shape that
fails `isValid`.

Tells whether the shape is well formed, which a successful operation does not always guarantee.

It checks that edges lie on their faces, wires and shells close, and tolerances agree. A fillet
too large for its faces fails; a shape passing through itself, such as a pipe wider than its
bends, passes. Large parts take a few hundred milliseconds.

join more than two faces. The shapes given are left as they were.

form `manifold.shapes.manifoldFromMesh` takes, so an OCCT solid can carry on as a Manifold

solid gives a closed mesh. `precision` is the meshing tolerance.

Triangulates a shape into a mesh for drawing: one entry per face with its vertices, normals,
UVs and triangle indexes, one per edge with its points, and the vertex points.

`precision` is the meshing tolerance in model units. `isoCurvesU` and `isoCurvesV` add each
face's iso curves as polylines, and `surfaceAnalysis` a value per vertex. A null shape gives
empty lists.

members.name: shapes
members.summary: Shape construction in OpenCascade, grouped by what you are building: vertices, edges, wires, faces, shells, solids and compounds.
members.doc:
Shape construction in OpenCascade, grouped by what you are building: vertices, edges, wires,
faces, shells, solids and compounds. The groups mirror the topological hierarchy, and a normal
modelling session climbs it - points become a wire, the wire becomes a face, the face is extruded
into a solid. Reach into the group for the kind you want rather than looking for one flat list.

members.doc:
Compounds in OpenCascade: a loose collection of shapes of any kind kept together as one shape, so
a set of parts can be moved, drawn or exported in one go. The shapes stay separate inside; a
compound does not fuse them. `shapes.shape` and the getters on the other shape classes take a
compound apart again.

members.summary: Edges in OpenCascade: single curves between two vertices, straight, circular, elliptical or free-form.
members.doc:
Edges in OpenCascade: single curves between two vertices, straight, circular, elliptical or
free-form. Build them from points and lines, as arcs, circles and ellipses, or as lines and circles
tangent to other curves in a plane; cut, lengthen and blend them; read them back as points,
lengths, tangents and centers; and pick edges out of any shape. Edges join end to end into wires,
which `shapes.wire` handles. Parameters along an edge run from 0 at its start to 1 at its end;
angles are in degrees.

members.name: face
members.summary: Faces in OpenCascade: bounded pieces of a surface, flat or curved, with an outer boundary wire and optional inner wires that make holes.
members.doc:
Faces in OpenCascade: bounded pieces of a surface, flat or curved, with an outer boundary wire
and optional inner wires that make holes. Build them from wires or surfaces, through point grids,
between or inside edges, or as ready-made flat shapes (circles, rectangles, stars, beam profiles)
that lie on the ground plane unless `direction` says otherwise; walk their surface through UV
parameters to get points, normals, iso curves and grids of wires; cut hole patterns into them, lay
them flat, and measure area and center of mass. U and V are the two directions of a surface, given
here as fractions from 0 to 1 of the face's own range. Faces join edge to edge into shells, which
`shapes.shell` handles.

curved style instead sweeps one along the other from a shared corner.

join as a compound of what did.

members.summary: Solids in OpenCascade: closed shapes that enclose a volume.
members.doc:
Solids in OpenCascade: closed shapes that enclose a volume. Build one from a primitive
(`createBox`, `createSphere`, `createCylinder`, `createCone`, `createTorus`), from a flat profile
extruded front and back (the star, n-gon, heart, beam and other profile solids), or from a closed
shell with `fromClosedShell`; then measure it with the volume, surface area and center of mass
getters, and filter points by whether they lie inside it. Vertices, edges, wires, faces, shells
and compounds have their own classes beside this one under `shapes`.

members.name: wire
members.summary: Wires in OpenCascade: chains of edges joined end to end, open like a path or closed like an outline.
members.doc:
Wires in OpenCascade: chains of edges joined end to end, open like a path or closed like an
outline. Build them from points and curves (polylines, B-splines, Beziers, interpolations,
helices, spirals), as ready-made flat outlines (circles, rectangles, stars, beam profiles, text)
that lie on the ground plane unless `direction` says otherwise, or by joining and splitting
existing edges and wires; read them back as points, tangents, lengths and centers; offset an open
one to one side; map, wrap or project them onto faces and shapes. Parameters along a wire run from
0 at its start to 1 at its end and follow each edge's own parameter, not distance. A closed wire is
what `shapes.face` fills to make a face.

winding, and the curve is approximated within `tolerance`.

`divideByEqualDistance` spaces the points by length rather than by parameter; with
`zigZagsPerEdge` true each edge gets its own zig-zag, so edge counts must match.

members.summary: Makes a smooth B-spline wire that passes through every point in order.
members.doc:
Makes a smooth B-spline wire that passes through every point in order.

`periodic` closes the curve so it is smooth across the seam, which gives nicely shaped loops.
`parametrization` controls the spacing between points: `centripetal` resists cusps and
overshoot when the points are uneven. `startTangent` and `endTangent`, or one `tangents`
entry per point, force the curve's direction there.

members.doc:
Makes a closed, smooth B-spline wire through the points whose shape is mirror-symmetric
whenever the points are, with no odd-looking start or end point.

A plain periodic `interpolatePoints` can look skewed at its seam for symmetric inputs such as
a square or a triangle; this variant does not. It fails with an error if the points cannot be
interpolated.

members.name: svg
members.summary: Importing SVG drawings as OpenCascade shapes.
members.doc:
Importing SVG drawings as OpenCascade shapes. The importer parses the document (paths, basic
shapes, transforms and the style cascade), reduces every element to the generic path vocabulary
of `path` and builds wires, and faces where it can, laid on the ground plane and placed by the
import options. `loadSVG` gives one compound for the whole drawing; `loadSVGStructured` gives one
shape per element with its fill and stroke.

rule, `nonzero` and `evenOdd` force a rule, `perSubpath` makes one face per closed subpath
without holes.

Parses an SVG document and builds every drawable element into one compound shape on the
ground plane, ready to draw, extrude or transform as a whole.

`faceStrategy` decides whether closed outlines become faces, `scale` and `flipY` map SVG
units and its downward Y axis, and `alignment`, `direction` and `center` place the result.
Invisible elements are skipped unless asked for.

members.name: transforms
members.summary: Moving, turning, scaling and mirroring OpenCascade shapes, and building the 4x4 matrices that describe such moves.
members.doc:
Moving, turning, scaling and mirroring OpenCascade shapes, and building the 4x4 matrices that
describe such moves. Every method returns a new shape and leaves the input as it was. Angles are
in degrees, distances in model units, and a rotation axis passes through the origin unless a
method takes a center. Matrices are 16 numbers in column-major order (the translation sits at
indices 12 to 14); a list of matrices is applied first to last as one combined move, which is how
`transformByMatrix` and the `...ToMatrix` builders fit together.

Rotates a shape about the origin by a quaternion given as `[x, y, z, w]`.

The quaternion is normalized first, so its length does not matter. Quaternions are what
animation and physics libraries hand out, so this saves converting them to an axis and an
angle.

The PlayCanvas side of the library: what lives in the rendered scene rather than in a CAD kernel.
The `camera` property builds and steers the orbit camera; drawing itself goes through `draw`, and
the plain data helpers sit beside it on the base object.

The orbiting camera for PlayCanvas: it looks at a pivot point from a distance and turns around it
with `yaw` around the vertical axis and `pitch` up or down, both in degrees. The controller it
gives back carries the camera entity and its input handlers; the methods here move the pivot,
frame an entity and reset the view.
