members.name: vectorChar

fields.name: char
fields.doc:
The character to draw; only its first character is used, and an unknown one is drawn as a
question mark.

fields.name: xOffset
fields.doc: How far to shift the strokes along X, in model units.

fields.name: yOffset
fields.doc:
How far to shift the strokes along the second axis of the character plane, in model
units.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: The height of a capital letter, in model units; the strokes are scaled to it.

fields.name: extrudeOffset
fields.doc:
A margin, in model units, taken off the height and split above and below, so an extruded
character keeps its full size.

members.summary: Draws one character as line paths with a simple stroke font.
members.doc:
Draws one character as line paths with a simple stroke font.

The paths lie flat on the XZ plane, scaled so the character is `height` tall, and are
returned with the character's width and height. An unknown character is drawn as a question
mark.
Example: 'A' at height 10 -> the strokes of an A, 10 units tall

members.name: vectorText

fields.name: text
fields.doc: The text to draw; a line break starts a new line.

fields.name: xOffset
fields.doc: How far to shift the whole block along X, in model units.

fields.name: yOffset
fields.doc: How far to shift the whole block along the second axis of the text plane, in model units.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: The height of a capital letter, in model units.

fields.name: lineSpacing
fields.doc:
The distance between lines as a multiple of the height; 1.4 leaves a little air between
them.

fields.name: letterSpacing
fields.doc:
Extra space between characters as a multiple of the height; 0 uses the font's own
spacing.

fields.name: align
fields.doc:
How lines of different length line up: at their left edge, their center or their right
edge.

fields.name: extrudeOffset
fields.doc:
A margin, in model units, taken off the height and split above and below each character,
so extruded text keeps its full size.

fields.name: centerOnOrigin
fields.doc: When true, the middle of the whole text block is moved to the origin.

members.summary: Draws a text, with line breaks, as line paths with a simple stroke font.
members.doc:
Draws a text, with line breaks, as line paths with a simple stroke font.

Each line comes back as its characters with their paths, laid out flat on the XZ plane with
the given height, spacing and alignment; `centerOnOrigin` puts the middle of the block at the
origin.
Example: 'Hello' at height 10 -> five characters with their strokes

The Three.js side of the library: what lives in the rendered scene rather than in a CAD kernel.
The `camera` property builds and steers the orbit camera; drawing itself goes through `draw`, and
the plain data helpers sit beside it on the base object.

members.name: orbitCamera
members.summary: The orbiting camera for Three.js: it looks at a pivot point from a distance and turns around it with `yaw` around the vertical axis and `pitch` up or down, both in degrees.
members.doc:
The orbiting camera for Three.js: it looks at a pivot point from a distance and turns around it
with `yaw` around the vertical axis and `pitch` up or down, both in degrees. The controller it
gives back carries the camera and its input handlers; the methods here move the pivot, frame an
object, reset the view and fence the distance and pitch.

Measures the angle from the first vector to the second, turning around a reference direction,
in degrees from 0 to 360.

The turn is counter-clockwise when the reference vector points toward you: a clockwise turn
of 30 degrees reads as 330.
Example: [1,0,0] to [0,0,-1] around [0,1,0] -> 90

members.name: span

fields.name: step
fields.doc:
Distance between neighboring numbers; the last number is `max` only when a step lands on
it.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: The first number of the span.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: The end of the span; included when a step lands on it.

members.summary: Lists the numbers from `min` to `max`, stepping by `step`; `max` is included when a step lands on it.
members.doc:
Lists the numbers from `min` to `max`, stepping by `step`; `max` is included when a step
lands on it.

Example: min=0, max=10, step=2 -> [0,2,4,6,8,10]

members.name: spanEaseItems

fields.name: nrItems
fields.doc: How many numbers to produce, including `min` and `max`; at least 2.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: The first number.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: The last number.

fields.name: ease
fields.doc:
The easing curve that spaces the numbers: an `easeIn` curve bunches them near `min`, an
`easeOut` curve near `max`, an `easeInOut` curve at both ends.

fields.name: intervals
fields.doc:
When true, the result holds the gaps between neighboring numbers instead of the numbers
themselves; the first entry is `min`.

members.summary: Lists `nrItems` numbers from `min` to `max` spaced by an easing curve, so they bunch up at one end or both.
members.doc:
Lists `nrItems` numbers from `min` to `max` spaced by an easing curve, so they bunch up at
one end or both.

With `intervals` on, the result holds the gaps between neighbors instead of the values
themselves.
Example: min=0, max=100, nrItems=5, ease='easeInQuad' -> [0, 6.25, 25, 56.25, 100]

members.name: spanLinearItems

fields.name: nrItems
fields.doc: How many numbers to produce, including `min` and `max`; at least 2.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: The first number.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: The last number.

members.summary: Lists `nrItems` evenly spaced numbers from `min` to `max`, both included.
members.doc:
Lists `nrItems` evenly spaced numbers from `min` to `max`, both included.

Example: min=0, max=10, nrItems=5 -> [0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10]

members.name: sub

fields.name: first
fields.doc:
First vector. Where order matters it is the left operand: the one subtracted from in
`sub`, the left side of the product in `cross`.

fields.name: second
fields.doc: Second vector, with the same number of entries as `first`.

members.summary: Subtracts the second vector from the first, entry by entry.
members.doc:
Subtracts the second vector from the first, entry by entry.

Example: [10,20,30] - [1,2,3] -> [9,18,27]

members.name: sum

fields.name: vector
fields.doc: The vector, as a list of numbers.

members.summary: Adds up all values of a vector into one number.
members.doc:
Adds up all values of a vector into one number.

Example: [1,2,3,4] -> 10

members.name: vectorXY

fields.name: x
fields.doc: The X value, the first entry.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: The Y value, the second entry.

members.summary: Builds a 2D vector from its x and y values.
members.doc:
Builds a 2D vector from its x and y values.

Example: x=3, y=4 -> [3,4]

members.name: vectorXYZ

fields.name: x
fields.doc: The X value, the first entry.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: The Y value, the second entry; Y is up.

fields.name: z
fields.doc: The Z value, the third entry.

members.summary: Builds a 3D vector from its x, y and z values.
members.doc:
Builds a 3D vector from its x, y and z values.

Example: x=1, y=2, z=3 -> [1,2,3]

members.name: vectorsTheSame

fields.name: vec1
fields.doc: First vector to compare.

fields.name: vec2
fields.doc: Second vector; a different length means the two are never the same.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.doc: Entries count as equal when they differ by less than this.

members.summary: Tells whether two vectors are the same within a tolerance, entry by entry.
members.doc:
Tells whether two vectors are the same within a tolerance, entry by entry.

Vectors of different length are never the same.
Example: [1,2,3] and [1.0001,2.0001,3.0001] with tolerance 0.001 -> true

Inputs.Base.basicAlignmentEnum.name: basicAlignmentEnum
Inputs.Base.basicAlignmentEnum.summary: Alignment against a nine-cell grid, combining a horizontal and a vertical position into one value - topLeft through bottomRight.

Inputs.Base.fogModeEnum.summary: How distance fog thickens: not at all, linearly between a start and an end distance, or exponentially - squared exponential being the densest.

Inputs.Base.gradientDirectionEnum.summary: The direction a linear gradient runs, given either as a named direction such as to bottom right or as an angle in degrees.

Inputs.Base.horizontalAlignEnum.summary: Horizontal alignment of content against its anchor: left, center or right.

Inputs.Math.mathTwoNrOperatorEnum.summary: The arithmetic operation applied to two numbers: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power or modulus.

Inputs.OCCT.approxParametrizationTypeEnu.summary: How points are spaced along a curve when it is approximated.

Inputs.OCCT.bRepOffsetModeEnum.summary: How an offset treats the original shape.

Inputs.OCCT.booleanStrategyEnum.name: booleanStrategyEnum

Inputs.OCCT.brepGraphNodeKindEnum.name: brepGraphNodeKindEnum

Inputs.OCCT.circleInclusionEnum.name: circleInclusionEnum

Inputs.OCCT.dimensionEndTypeEnum.name: dimensionEndTypeEnum
Inputs.OCCT.dimensionEndTypeEnum.summary: How a dimension line terminates: with nothing, or with an arrowhead.

Inputs.OCCT.directionEnum.summary: Which side of the original geometry an operation works on: outside, inside, or centerd on it.

Inputs.OCCT.dxfAcadVersionEnum.summary: Which AutoCAD DXF version to write.

Inputs.OCCT.featureExtentEnum.name: featureExtentEnum
Inputs.OCCT.featureExtentEnum.summary: How far a boss or a pocket runs from its sketch face.

Inputs.OCCT.fileTypeEnum.name: fileTypeEnum
Inputs.OCCT.fileTypeEnum.summary: The CAD interchange format for import and export: STEP or IGES.

Inputs.OCCT.fillingStyleEnum.name: fillingStyleEnum
Inputs.OCCT.fillingStyleEnum.summary: How a patch fills between its boundary edges.

Inputs.OCCT.gccEntPositionEnum.name: gccEntPositionEnum

Inputs.OCCT.surfaceAnalysisEnum.summary: What a surface analysis shows at each point of a face.
